one of you kicks the comforter off at 2 a.m. the other wakes up an hour later pulling it back. mismatched sleep temperatures are a common bedroom compromise. but you don't necessarily have to choose between sharing a bed and being comfortable in it.

4 dual-zone bed approaches, compared: • two separate comforters: budget, silent, no active heating or cooling • dual-control heated pad: mid-range, warms only • bedjet 3: premium, warms or cools via airflow, audible fan • water-circulating pad: premium, both on many systems

common mistake: buying a heated pad when one of you runs hot. "off" means no added warmth, not cool. better approach: match the setup to the gap. only one runs cold? dual-control heated pad. only one runs hot? lighter comforter on that side. both? that's where bedjet fits.

red-eye, the usual way: you drift off. your head drops. you jolt awake. repeat until landing. then the hotel room is too bright and too loud to catch up on sleep. that's not one problem. it's three, showing up at three different times.

a red-eye comfort kit, in three parts: - in the seat: a neck pillow so a head-drop is less likely to wake you - after landing: a compact massage gun, used at the hotel, not on the plane - at the hotel: sleep mask, earplugs, portable white noise you may only need one piece.

before: a squishy microbead u-pillow that flattens, and your head still drops forward. after: matching the shape to how you sit. lean on the window? a full collar, or a wrap-style on that side. sit upright in a middle or aisle seat? look for front or chin support.

pitch-black room. total silence. then a phone alarm at full volume. you're awake, but it feels more like being startled than waking up. a sunrise alarm clock changes how that moment starts: the room gets lighter first, and sound follows only if you want it.

3 sunrise alarm clocks, compared: • hatch restore: light + built-in sounds + app routines, premium • philips smartsleep: on-device buttons on many models, radio on some • lumie bodyclock: light-first wake, on-device controls on many models optional membership: hatch only.

common mistake: assuming every model in a line works the same. better: check the exact listing for • light-only wake (if you share a bed) • how quietly the sound starts • whether setup needs an app want your phone off the nightstand? start with button-based models.
